stateVocabulary.ENABLED_V1: Ships in v1, to every user, with the stated coverage and the stated uncertainty rendered.
stateVocabulary.INTERNAL_EXPERIMENTAL: Runs, is measured, is never reachable by a user in v1. No public surface, no marketing claim.
stateVocabulary.DISABLED_NOT_READY: The gap is OURS — code, coverage, or an unmeasured property. Closing it is our work.
stateVocabulary.DISABLED_EXTERNAL_BLOCK: The gap is NOT ours — an authorization, a credential, a registrar's answer. No amount of our work closes it.
stateVocabulary.POST_V1: Deliberately out of v1 scope. Not a gap.
stateVocabulary.ENABLED_V1_KILLABLE: Ships in v1 on this platform, AND carries a capability kill switch that can disable it on this platform alone without disabling the capabilities named in `mustNotDisable`. Used where a platform policy risk is real but unproven.
stateVocabulary.OUT_OF_SCOPE_CURRENT_FOUNDER: Not a v1 product platform or surface by current explicit founder instruction. capabilities.coverageDefinition: MEASURED across six narrowing scopes of one query ('bail'). ADMITTED: one named court + 3 days -> 5 results in 154.6 ms; one named court + 1 month -> 5 results in 418.1 ms. REFUSED: one named court + 8 months; courts:[hc] category + 1 month at 262.6 ms; courts:[hc] + 29 days at 207.4 ms; unfiltered at 2.9 ms. Narrow control 'anticipatory bail cheque dishonour' + courts:[hc] + 29 days -> 5 results in 78.8 ms.
capabilities.whyNotReady: SUPERSEDED IN R14, AND THE MECHANISM WAS RESTATED. R13 said, reading retrieve.ts at the Day-0 seal, that 'filters is a parameter of that same function and is NOT consulted before the refusal', so 'the bound is corpus-wide while the query is not'. READ FROM CURRENT HEAD 19920c0f that is no longer the mechanism. ADMISSION IS POPULATION-SHAPED, in two stages: (1) the corpus-wide lexeme document-frequency ceiling runs first and admits outright if the rarest lexeme is discriminating enough; (2) ONLY IF that refuses, and ONLY IF the request carries a narrowing filter (court, courts, dateFrom, dateTo or caseType), the server COUNTS the eligible population with the same predicates the ranker will apply, stopping early at a cap, and admits when the population is at or under it. A capped probe proves only 'at least the cap' and never admits - unknown is not small. An admitted query is then ranked inside a MATERIALIZED fence so the structured predicates run before the text index.
capabilities.stateChangedBy: NEW3 R13, 30 August 2026, on backend d96147e (rankWithinBoundedPopulation). R14 corrected the MECHANISM description on this row from current HEAD (population-shaped admission; a category filter narrows but not enough). capabilities.knownLimit: A COURT CATEGORY IS NARROWING - IT IS JUST NOT NARROWING ENOUGH. R13 said 'a court CATEGORY is not narrowing', and that wording is mechanically false at HEAD: the eligible-population probe treats `courts` (the category form) as a narrowing filter exactly like `court`, and counts the real population it selects. courts:[hc] is still REFUSED because every High Court is a population far above the cap, not because the filter was ignored. The consequence for the refusal screen is unchanged and still binding: offer a single named court and a shorter date range, and do not present a category chip as THE REMEDY for a too-broad refusal.

notEnumeratedHere.rule: This registry enumerates the capabilities v1 SHIPS or has adjudicated. Its schema does not require exhaustive enumeration of every capability the product does not have, and adding rows for absent features would invent a feature taxonomy in a Gate-B convergence round.
notEnumeratedHere.drafting: Document drafting has NO row. It is absent by prohibition, not by oversight: no generation capability is ENABLED, generation.evidence_from_passages is POST_V1 on every platform, and no drafting claim is permitted by the claims register.
notEnumeratedHere.hearingPack: Hearing Pack has NO row, for the same reason, and briefing.daily_loop - the nearest shipped-adjacent thing - is DISABLED_NOT_READY on every platform.
notEnumeratedHere.classification: NON_GATE_P1_BACKLOG. Neither absence blocks Gate B and neither authorises a claim. If a future round decides the registry must enumerate absent capabilities, that is a schema decision and gets its own CCR.
